title: Mirrors at Spano's and Savocas; pay and Sweet Lucy wine
summary: Comparison of Spano's mirror with Savocas, band size, and musicians paid with a few hours and all the wine they could drink.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: His Spanos, the tonk that had the mirror in it?
Yeah, that's right. It had a mirror, a long mirror, because all the women that's coming in and dancing, they all would look to see themselves dancing. That big, long mirror in there.
How about Savokas? You mentioned Savokas.

Well, Savokas had mirrors in there, but they didn't have those sort of mirrors, you see. At Spanos, they had the piano right in the corner, and they had the mirror right there, while the people come in there, the women, they start dancing, see themselves dancing. But at Savokas, it was different. The only mirror that you could see yourself is the bartender, you know, I mean the glasses. The bartender.
Did you play the piano Savokas?

Savokas? No, not me. The other guys played the piano. It always was the piano playing. At that time, musicians, they wasn't getting them, it was about two or three hours, and all the wine he could drink. They had a wine they used to drink, they called a Sweet Lucy. Sweet Lucy, black wine, sweet, sweet, sweet syrup. It was called a Sweet Lucy wine, that's the kind of wine they was drinking at that time.
What kind of band did they have in Savokas? How many pieces?

Years worth? Well, sometimes they'd have four pieces, three pieces, sometimes five pieces. And so on like that. But most of the time they had a piano player, just a piano player. Sometime a guy would come in there and play guitar and sing, and he'd get with the piano player.
